### 2026-10-27: I made the potential part spreadsheet of what will go on the device. Despite arduous searching, I can't seem to make all the components draw less than the highest grade coin battery's max current draw

**3h**

I made the potential part spreadsheet of what will go on the device. Despite arduous searching, I can't seem to make all the components draw less than the highest grade coin battery's max current draw. I never knew coin batteries sucked so much for current draw... I might have to resort to not making it a business card and it'll be encased with a small lipo pouch... Yes this actually took me more than 3 hours of research but lowk don't have more than 3  images.
I just reading MicroSD alone draws more current than most coin batteries can provide...

### 2026-11-03: I made more changes to the PCB as I realized I had a couple mistakes when back-checking with datasheets and Gemini. I was missing a few decoupling capacitors like next to the DAC and the output side o

**6h**

I made more changes to the PCB as I realized I had a couple mistakes when back-checking with datasheets and Gemini. I was missing a few decoupling capacitors like next to the DAC and the output side of the linear regulator:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/89db269443252f8e0a0d2ae553f7800e1d66a59523f6cbb9057ad8c0311e7aa8.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/b72032878647390c9128223c74d80f28135430db1436e270b55740311614f76a.png)

I had also changed my 50uF capacitors to 47uF ones since 50uF capacitors I've realized aren't standard.
I also added a P-channel MOSFET to the Micro-SD card in order to save as much power as possible when it's not needed. I decided to use a P-Channel instead of a N-Channel since the GPIO pins on the pico aren't high enough above 3v3 to fully open the gate, and if I put it between GND and VSS then that would introduce problems with voltage floating upwards due to the command line pins.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/1147f8f9fab7f0f77cd46d2725732a7af0e56425711e470771c5913cf60fca54.png)

I also changed the MOSFET type to be one that can be controlled to fully open/close with a pico 2's voltage and is still a basic part on JLCPCB.

Upon reading the datasheet again, I realized that the STAT1 and STAT2 pins are actually voltage sinks and not sources. Thus I had to turn them around and tie their anodes to 5v5 instead:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/a01b3287b3e79c5812b42830c58a6a5d5ab348a01e07d76baf4cdb0e5cabe8a5.png)

I had also realized that I wasn't actually dividing my voltage correctly to get a battery reading through the ADC pin. Apparently ADC pins draw practically 0 current so the voltage drop is pretty much 0 if it's not also tied to ground like so:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/6b178384a377f7c44e1766ddbe38fd31d7819399c88e357968a3124f00e3c71b.png)

These changes introduced a TON of new ERC checker errors, like around 30, and I had to clean them all up again. A lot of them were actually related to my kicad crashing occasionally and messing up the custom library dependencies when i middle click for some reason. Likely another linux issue.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/6376b335f1d1b5dbe8585c2cb3f06898881a3d43a458df818c730d4b9f8db248.png)

### 2026-11-03: I started wiring the PCB. I know this looks like TERRIBLE wiring, but I REALLY wanted the MCU right next to the screen for aesthetics. Wouldn't it just look terrible if the pico was like, in the middl

**5h**

I started wiring the PCB. I know this looks like TERRIBLE wiring, but I REALLY wanted the MCU right next to the screen for aesthetics. Wouldn't it just look terrible if the pico was like, in the middle of the board? Also it's just a lot more fun this way. I think I'm going to have to rewire this though. I had considered moving my pins around, but there were actually a lot more trade-offs than one might think. For example, If I moved the display pins from the top side to the left, then the pins involved with the buttons would need to go on the top and that would be even more of a nightmare to wire. I've never used so many via traces in my life.

I also went ahead and roughly 3D Modeled the LCD HS096T01H13 screen for some reason. Don't ask why, I just felt like it.
https://cad.onshape.com/documents/67362369f60f85328142f508/w/f18d904090de24c64018daa0/e/3137deeed35128d6fdb7bcc3?renderMode=0&uiState=6aea2d6badfa518caef30817

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/A1g9crjQinL4h8m4FayIpcASMHZiPgLG/1af8177aafc4d996a4e11a5858f088fb584e31621bfcdb407202db31bb98710c.png)

Before you see it, I want to say that this was an absolute nightmare to wire. I think I'm going to have to rewire everything again after this since I'm still missing a connection to ground with one of the pins and a 3v3 connection but I can't since the area around it is already so crowded with vias. I think I'm going to have to switch some pins around on the rp2350 and make it so the schematic is uglyyyy urgh.
Okay here, I went ahead and wired everything:
